transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-28
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Cole (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (Aurelia Head of Cloud), Sonia Patel (NetOps), Ravi Menon (CTO)

Summary (auto): weekly POC check-in — review of load test artifacts, kernel/quantization upgrade fallout, and cutover playbook review.

[00:00] Ethan Cole: okay hi everyone thanks for joining, um we'll do quick rollcall and then jump into the test results. priya are you on audio?
[00:05] Priya Nair: yeah i'm here, hi all. i pulled the artifacts from the run earlier and i've got the tail-percentiles and the node-level logs.
[00:12] Jared Kim: good, we had a noisy morning but i'm ready. sonia is on the call as well.
[00:15] Sonia Patel: yep hi. quick note our oncall window is open till 17:30 so we should be conscious of that.
[00:20] Ethan Cole: perfect. quick agenda: results summary, kernel/quant upgrade failures, proposed cutover playbook, fallback routing, and security gating. we'll leave five to ten for next steps. sound good?
[00:30] Ravi Menon: sounds fine.

--- Results review ---
[00:35] Priya Nair: ok so i'll start. during last friday's 1.5 hour ramp run we pushed a 3x burst to simulate morning surge. overall qps held but we saw 99.9 spikes up to 420ms from baseline 120ms on CPU-backed nodes, and on the dedicated GPUs the p99 climbed to ~310ms when the kv cache warmed cold. so pattern is consistent with prefix cache warm-up and a small tail amplification during spikes.
[01:05] Sonia Patel: yeah we saw that on the telemetry too, the first 40 requests after a idle period were notably slower. is that the kv cache miss behavior?
[01:12] Priya Nair: exactly — the runtime currently rehydrates the kv pages on first token lookups; we have a prefix cache plan that should reduce that but we also saw the kernel upgrade candidate caused one worker to segfault mid-run which amplified the issue because traffic landed on a few nodes.
[01:30] Ethan Cole: quick clarification — which kernel candidate did you run, priya? the 0.9.8 quantized kernel?
[01:36] Priya Nair: yeah 0.9.8-quant-opt, it's the one that improves memory pressure and helps CPU latency at the cost of a very small change in decoding timing. most runs were fine but one node had a nvml OOM and then a tidy crash, looks like driver interplay. logs attached in the artifacts folder.
[01:55] Jared Kim: oh — nvml OOM, so that points to a driver mismatch probably with the customer's custom AMI? we patched drivers last month though.
[02:03] Priya Nair: right, and that node was using an older nvidia runtime. i think we hit an edge case.

[02:10] Sonia Patel: important for us: what's the blast radius if that happens in production? we have strict SLA windows.
[02:15] Ethan Cole: good question. our cutover playbook assumes we do a rolling canary: 5% traffic on canary nodes for 30 minutes, health checks, then 20%, etc. if a node crashes we have automated circuit-breaker routing to the hosted Redwood tier for overflow which keeps the service up albeit at slightly higher latency/cost. that's the immediate rollback path.
[02:40] Ravi Menon: fallback to hosted is acceptable for emergency but we need to quantify egress and cost for compliance. can you share the published cost delta?
[02:48] Ethan Cole: yes — for your workload the delta ballpark is +25% per-token cost when routed to hosted as compared to your dedicated reserved capacity. i'll send a small showback table after this call.

--- Kernel/Upgrade remediation ---
[03:05] Priya Nair: remediation plan is: revert the 0.9.8 kernel on nodes with older driver, add a preflight check in the upgrade job to validate driver/AMI compatibility, and push a hotfix build that traps nvml OOMs and fails gracefully without core dump. i'm targeting that hotfix tonight and will run a smoke on canary tomorrow.
[03:28] Sonia Patel: can you also add an automated step to surface kernel mismatch in the console before we accept the upgrade? a simple compatibility check would have saved the run.
[03:36] Priya Nair: yes, we'll add a pre-upgrade compatibility gate and a one-click revert.

--- Cutover playbook (detailed) ---
[03:45] Ethan Cole: i'll walk through the proposed cutover playbook: 1) prep: freeze model version and snapshot KV caches, 2) canary deploy (5% traffic for 30 min with ttr health checks), 3) run 2-hour load test at 60% of peak, 4) progressive ramp to 50/80/100%, with 15min observation windows, 5) final verification and annealing period. explicit rollback: traffic shift to hosted tier plus immediate kernel revert.
[04:20] Jared Kim: what's the expected blackout window for the canary? we need to inform our incident responders.
[04:26] Ethan Cole: if all goes well, zero blackout. worst case, a single node crash results in a small uptick in latency for affected sessions for up to two minutes while circuit-breaker reroutes. we'll capture that in the runbook.
[04:36] Ravi Menon: and what's the telemetry retention during the test? we need 90 days for forensic, can you commit to that?
[04:44] Priya Nair: by default we keep 30 days on the POC cluster but for this pilot we can enable extended retention to 90 days for audit logs; it will cost a bit more. i'll mark that as part of the runbook and pricing note.

[05:00] Sonia Patel: we also need the audit trail for each rollout action (who triggered, artifact checksums). is that in the console?
[05:06] Ethan Cole: yes — the private control plane publishes audit logs with user identity (SSO), action, timestamp, and artifact checksum. they can be routed to your SIEM. we'll include a sample export.

--- Telemetry gaps & test instrumentation ---
[05:20] Priya Nair: one gap we hit: missing kv cache miss counters at the per-prefix level — we currently have node-level misses but not per-prefix. for next test we will add per-prefix instrumentation and a short-lived tag that surfaces cold-warm transitions so you can see the warmup curve.
[05:38] Sonia Patel: that will help. also can we get a heatmap of request affinity by model shard? we've seen uneven distribution in earlier canaries.
[05:45] Priya Nair: yes we'll add request affinity metrics and a shard distribution report.

--- Security & compliance ---
[05:55] Ethan Cole: quick security check: where do we stand on KMS/HSM acceptance and SAML?
[05:59] Jared Kim: security wants KMS with key wrap and rotation policy; SAML SSO is already on their side but we need to validate SCIM provisioning.
[06:07] Priya Nair: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS; we'll provide integration docs and a test harness for key rotation. Regarding SCIM, we can do a staged sync — I'll put steps in the security bundle.
[06:16] Ravi Menon: one ask: we need proof of SOC2 + pen test summary before production cutover. is that bundle ready?
[06:22] Ethan Cole: yes, we have current SOC2 and a redacted pen test summary; i'll attach them with the security bundle.

--- Cost & routing tradeoffs ---
[06:30] Sonia Patel: circling back to cost: if we need to use hosted fallback during a high-traffic incident, is there a throttling plan to avoid runaway bills?
[06:38] Ethan Cole: yes we can set an egress quota per-customer and per-route; the system alerts at 50/75/90%. also the fallback routing is capped by your configured burst allowance.
[06:48] Jared Kim: good. we will want the default to fail closed to prevent unknown costs in the event of runaway.
[06:52] Priya Nair: we can make the fallback policy explicit in the runbook: allow fallback only during business-hours incidents and with manual approval for cost-sensitive customers.

--- Questions from Customer ---
[07:00] Sonia Patel: how long to validate the hotfix on canary before we consider gradual rollout?
[07:05] Priya Nair: target is a 2-hour smoke then 30 minutes at 5% canary, but we recommend a 2-hour load window after that before hitting 20%.
[07:13] Ravi Menon: if the hotfix still causes a segmentation issue, do you have a debug plan? we can't have iterative crashes during a business day.
[07:20] Priya Nair: yes — debug path is to collect minidumps, isolate the workload to a smaller set of tokens, and revert to prior kernel. the automated job will not roll to more than one batch until health checks pass.

--- Misc/Observations ---
[07:30] Ethan Cole: small note — during the run we saw a non-deterministic delay when token sequence lengths exceeded 1,024 for a minority of requests; not sure if that's model-level or runtime. priya will instrument sequence-length buckets.
[07:45] Priya Nair: right, adding that to the instrumentation list.

--- Recap & explicit next steps ---
[07:55] Ethan Cole: recap: priya does hotfix and smoke by 2026-04-29, ethan will send the cutover runbook and cost showback by 2026-04-30, sonia to confirm maintenance window. security bundle + SOC2 docs out 2026-04-30. agreed?
[08:12] Jared Kim: yes confirmed, i'll get the window 2nd May tentative.
[08:18] Sonia Patel: i'll share test creds by tomorrow.
[08:20] Ravi Menon: thanks all. one last thing — can we have a war-room contact list in the runbook? prefer names and cell numbers for the roll.
[08:28] Ethan Cole: absolutely i'll append a war-room contact list.

[08:35] Priya Nair: closing note — i'll annotate the artifacts with the node-level logs and the per-request traces for the spike period, so you can triage offline.
[08:44] Ethan Cole: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the runbook and the hotfix status.
[08:49] Jared Kim: thanks. bye.
[08:51] Meeting end.
